column1: # Character creation's own prompts, which the suite has never verified.
# From the unverified 217 of `scenario_literal_coverage.py`: `By what name
# shalt thou be known?`, `Art thou Male or Female?`, `Keep this name?`,
# `Keep same sex?` and `Enter new name:` have never appeared in a sampled
# stock frame. `chargen-journey-basics` walks past them but its beats sample
# later, and from the first virtue question on that scenario is drawing at
# random - `chargen.md` picks the virtue pair per question - so it carries a
# marker phrase that makes the comparator treat its differences as
# non-results.
# These prompts come before that draw and are fully deterministic, so they
# can be compared even though the questions after them cannot. This header
# deliberately avoids the comparator's marker vocabulary - the first revision
# tripped it in the very sentence explaining why the later beats are not
# comparable, and the whole scenario read as a non-result. This stops on each of
# them in turn and goes no further.
# `chargen.md` Section 3 puts the name prompt first, then the sex prompt,
# then the confirmations.
# **Its panel count is not a result.** During character creation the region
# the comparator decodes as the roster panel is the title artwork, and the
# "Warriors of Destiny" flame inside it animates - so all three beats report
# panel differences that are animation phase in a region that holds no roster
# at all. The message window, which is what this scenario exists to verify,
# agrees on every beat. Left visible rather than suppressed: a marker phrase
# would silence the message-window comparison too.
# No shot of the start menu: its "Warriors of Destiny" flame is a running
# animation, so the two sides catch it in different phases and the beat
# cannot agree. That is the title screen rather than anything this scenario
# covers.
